title: @escaping: Store Callbacks
hints: A closure you store for later must be marked `@escaping`.
Keep an array of `(String) -> Void` handlers; `publish` loops over them.
jsBridge: In JS every callback can be stored for later. Swift makes you mark those parameters `@escaping`. Non-escaping closures (the default) can't outlive the call, which lets the compiler skip reference counting and makes `self` capture rules looser.

compass.q: JS never distinguishes "called now" from "stored for later" callbacks. What bugs does Swift's `@escaping` annotation surface (retain cycles, reentrancy)?
Why must you write `self.` explicitly inside escaping closures but not in non-escaping ones?
Stored callbacks vs Combine subjects vs `AsyncStream`: which handles unsubscribe best?
An event bus that stores handlers forever leaks. How do you design unsubscription (tokens, `weak` observers)?
